sections.heading: B — messages and litter
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience and scope
The audience is an Rhode Island first-time passenger-car applicant studying messages and litter. Use the exact selected source pages, plain definitions, complete qualifiers and the distinction between a source snapshot and a current official rule. Commercial operation and road-test maneuver grading remain outside this written-study scope.

sections.heading: C — messages and litter
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing and examination knowledge
FACT_ID: sec01-F001 | anchor: P2
A driver accepts responsibility for protecting other people as well as themselves whenever they use a vehicle.

FACT_ID: sec01-F002 | anchor: P2
Traffic laws and road rules serve to keep road users safe.

FACT_ID: sec01-F003 | anchor: P2
Looking away to read a message or handle a phone call can put the driver and surrounding people in danger.

FACT_ID: sec01-F004 | anchor: P2
Driving after alcohol or drug impairment endangers both the driver and other road users and is unlawful.

FACT_ID: sec01-F005 | anchor: P2
Drowsiness makes driving dangerous even when alcohol is not involved.

FACT_ID: sec01-F006 | anchor: P2
Wearing a seat belt is described as the most effective individual step for protection during a crash.

FACT_ID: sec01-F007 | anchor: P2
Children need to be secured in a restraint appropriate for their size.

FACT_ID: sec01-F008 | anchor: P2
Drivers should follow speed limits because excessive speed is involved in many serious crashes.

FACT_ID: sec01-F009 | anchor: P2
A careful driver still needs to watch others because their behavior cannot be controlled.

FACT_ID: sec01-F010 | anchor: P3
An applicant can choose to register as an organ donor when applying for a license.

FACT_ID: sec01-F011 | anchor: P3
Choosing donor registration does not change the medical care the person receives.

FACT_ID: sec01-F012 | anchor: P3
Organ donation creates no donation expense for the donor or the donor's family.

FACT_ID: sec01-F013 | anchor: P3
The handbook describes major religions as supporting donation or allowing it as a personal decision.

FACT_ID: sec01-F014 | anchor: P3
United States law forbids the sale or purchase of organs intended for transplantation.

FACT_ID: sec01-F015 | anchor: P4
Rhode Island's Division of Motor Vehicles operates within the state's Department of Revenue.

FACT_ID: sec01-F016 | anchor: P4
The DMV administers vehicle titling, registration and driver licensing laws under its Registrar's direction.

FACT_ID: sec01-F017 | anchor: P4
Driver testing and the issuance of operator licenses are among the DMV's responsibilities.

FACT_ID: sec01-F018 | anchor: P4
The DMV also administers motor vehicle insurance laws and vehicle inspection responsibilities.

FACT_ID: sec01-F019 | anchor: P4
The Community College of Rhode Island runs the statewide driver-education program.

FACT_ID: sec01-F020 | anchor: P4
The Community College of Rhode Island manages alcohol-education and defensive-driving retraining programs.

FACT_ID: sec01-F021 | anchor: P5
Litter includes deliberately discarded waste, such as food wrappers or cigarette ends thrown out by road users.

FACT_ID: sec01-F022 | anchor: P5
Waste released unintentionally through overflowing bins or unsecured loads also counts as litter.

FACT_ID: sec01-F023 | anchor: P5
Debris from damaged vehicles can become roadway litter.

FACT_ID: sec01-F024 | anchor: P5
Litter damages tourism, property values and residents' pride in their community.

FACT_ID: sec01-F025 | anchor: P5
Discarded waste can contaminate soil, water and air and harm the surrounding ecosystem.

FACT_ID: sec01-F026 | anchor: P5
Animals can swallow litter as food or become caught in it, with injury or death as possible results.

FACT_ID: sec01-F027 | anchor: P5
Breaking litter into microplastics can release harmful substances into the food chain and drinking water.

FACT_ID: sec01-F028 | anchor: P5
Removing litter becomes harder and more costly as the material breaks into smaller pieces.

FACT_ID: sec01-F029 | anchor: P5
Roadside litter can contribute to pooled water or become airborne and obstruct a driver's view.

FACT_ID: sec01-F030 | anchor: P5
Keeping waste contained inside the vehicle helps prevent litter from reaching the road.

FACT_ID: sec01-F031 | anchor: P5
Loads in a truck bed should be secured so that loose material cannot scatter onto roads.

FACT_ID: sec01-F032 | anchor: P5
Check for loose waste before driving with a window or sunroof open.

FACT_ID: sec01-F033 | anchor: P5
The driver's manual contains information used for the knowledge examination and driving-skills test.

FACT_ID: sec01-F034 | anchor: P5
Keep the manual accessible after licensing so that you can consult it again.

Misconceptions: Treat closely related requirements as separate rules; preserve the triggering condition and any exception given in each fact [P2].
Mnemonics: Remember the condition together with the required action; this is an authored study cue.
Glossary: Definitions in the fact blocks keep the source context rather than substituting a broader rule.
Dynamic isolation: Source thresholds remain snapshot-specific until current official reconciliation.

## C2 — Licensing and examination knowledge
FACT_ID: sec01-F035 | anchor: P5
The handbook provides driving guidance and information about laws but is not itself a legal document.

FACT_ID: sec01-F036 | anchor: P5
Use the DMV or Rhode Island legislature website to check changes in laws, procedures and fees.

FACT_ID: sec01-F037 | anchor: P6
New permit holders are encouraged to gain extensive supervised experience behind the wheel.

FACT_ID: sec01-F038 | anchor: P6
A responsible driver keeps their own seat belt fastened and ensures passengers are buckled up.

FACT_ID: sec01-F039 | anchor: P6
Avoid reading electronic messages as well as sending texts while driving.

FACT_ID: sec01-F040 | anchor: P6
Drivers need to respect pedestrians and other motorists sharing the road.

FACT_ID: sec01-F041 | anchor: P7
A driver is accountable for the safety of passengers and the public as well as their own safety.

FACT_ID: sec01-F042 | anchor: P7
Studying the manual helps with knowledge-test preparation, while safe habits require ongoing practice.

Handoff hints: Group the cited facts by their actual subject and condition. Use prerequisite relations only where one stated definition is needed to understand another fact.
